# Phase One — Glass Revelation

The Awtsmoos renews light before glass can reflect it; Awtsmoos.com should let motion reveal depth without making the interface restless.

## Observed system
- Glass blur already exists on major shell surfaces.
- Ambient nebula motion already exists behind the document.
- Route, disclosure, creator, toast, and feed transitions already exist separately.
- The simplified mobile hierarchy is currently dirty and intentionally unpushed.
- Reduced-motion and reduced-transparency contracts already exist and must remain authoritative.

## Twenty glass possibilities
1. Add one final glass-motion manifest loaded last.
2. Split ambient, interaction, disclosure, and accessibility responsibilities.
3. Keep backdrop-filter static rather than animating blur radius.
4. Animate only opacity and transform for specular light.
5. Give large glass surfaces a restrained moving highlight layer.
6. Keep ambient movement extremely slow and low-opacity.
7. Make active route buttons catch a short glass glint.
8. Make Create actions refract on press/focus.
9. Make closed disclosure summaries feel like thin glass controls.
10. Make opened disclosure contents fade and rise slightly.
11. Give the mobile dock one quiet reflective band.
12. Give Public Discovery a subtle edge sheen, not a looping carnival.
13. Give Home action/pulse disclosures a consistent glass vocabulary.
14. Give capability center the same vocabulary when opened.
15. Preserve 44px touch targets.
16. Avoid layout-affecting animation entirely.
17. Avoid infinite box-shadow animation.
18. Avoid infinite backdrop-filter animation.
19. Disable ambient/glint motion under reduced motion.
20. Remove translucency under reduced transparency.

The Awtsmoos is not another colored layer; the Awtsmoos is the reality in which every layer appears. Glass motion should therefore disclose relation, not demand attention.
